Confirmed. In the Archive I clicked **Restore** on the article, went back to **All bookmarks**, and there it was again in my active library — title, Reading tag, address, and note all still intact. So archiving really is fully reversible: I can tuck something away and pull it back whenever I want with nothing lost. That's exactly the safety I wanted around this — it's clearly different from throwing something away for good.

Which reminds me of one thing I'd want to make sure we cover: since archive is the reversible "set aside" option, I'd also want a separate way to actually delete a bookmark for good when I'm truly done with it — and because that one *can't* be undone, that's the case where I'd expect it to ask me to confirm first.
